one_month_reasoning: Dycom's own Q3 FY27 report is outside the window: Investing.com lists 24 Nov 2026 [18], after the 2026-11-08 cutoff. In-window events are read-throughs. Loudoun County votes on Oct 20 on an up-to-12-month pause of legislative data-center and substation approvals, retroactive to Sep 15 [12]. It has been telegraphed since Sep 17 and does not touch by-right or in-backlog work, so I expect little price impact. MasTec reports Q3 around Oct 29 [11]; its Communications EBITDA margin fell 170 bp to 8.2% in Q2 [10], so a further margin decline there would be a negative read for Dycom's segment, while stabilisation would help. AT&T, Verizon, Comcast and Charter report Q3 in late October with possible 2027 capex comments; the top four were ~58% of FY26 revenue [5]. None of these gives me a directional edge. Momentum is negative (down 52% from the high, close $269.23 just above the $263.36 low [18]); September open-market insider buys at $280-297 [13][14][15] and the buyback [2] lean the other way. I use a lognormal at the usual monthly volatility (52%/3.5 = 14.9%) with the median a hair below spot at $268.5.

EBITDA at Oct 2027 = $12.54B EV, less ~$2.56B lease-inclusive net debt, over 30.2M shares = $331. Blend 0.6 x 324 + 0.4 x 331 = $327.

bear.story: The H2 FY27 Communications flatness is a cycle turn rather than timing. FY28 Communications grows only +2% plus ~$100M of the wireless recapture ($6.17B) at a 12.5% margin (peer MasTec's segment margin already fell 170 bp in a quarter [10]). Building Systems is flat-ish ($1.68B) at 17% as the 24.5% Q2 margin, helped by estimate changes, normalises and DMV permitting pauses [12] slow new awards. The supplier-finance balance ($367.4M [9]) stops growing or unwinds, so FCF disappoints and interest stays ~$155M. EBITDA ~$1,057M gives FY28 adj. EPS ~$15.5 and NTM ~$16.1. At 11.5x NTM (below the 15.75x peer low, typical of a contractor with falling estimates; judgment) the price is ~$185.

base.story: The ~$150M wireless deferral returns in FY28 and underlying Communications grows ~6%, close to the H2 FY27 exit rate ex-53rd week. Building Systems margins settle at ~19%. FY28 adj. EPS ~$19.0, below the $20.78 consensus, so estimates drift down rather than collapse. The multiple stays compressed at ~15.5x NTM EPS of ~$20.3 (below my 16x fair multiple because the cash-quality question is unresolved until FCF shows without supplier-finance help), giving ~$315.

bull.story: Consensus is right: the $12.24B backlog (+53%) converts, FY28 EPS beats $20.78 (~$21.5) and FY29 reaches ~$24.5 (judgment, +14%). NTM EPS ~$23.8 re-rates toward MasTec's ~19-20x: 19 x 23.8 = ~$450.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: I dropped AGX (power-plant EPC) and APG (fire/life-safety services) after the supervisor review: neither shares Dycom's end markets closely enough. I keep LMB, against the supervisor: it is a mechanical/electrical contractor for critical facilities, the nearest listed analogue to Building Systems, and size is not a reason to exclude it. Fewer than 10 peers is unavoidable because few listed US contractors share Dycom's telecom mix. The discount is argued from verified facts that will persist through the horizon: (1) Leverage: net debt/TTM EBITDA ~2.9x for DY (StockAnalysis $2.70B / $0.932B) vs ~2.2x for MTZ ($2.92B / $1.31B) [19][21]; several high-multiple peers have far less debt. (2) Concentration: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen were 35.8% of Q2 revenue and the top four ~58% of FY26, on MSAs terminable for convenience with no volume commitment [2][5]. (3) Cash quality: supplier-finance obligations rose from $0 (Jul 2025) to $367.4M (Aug 2026) [9], FY26 OCF included a $223.2M accounts-payable increase [5], and receivables are sold non-recourse to a bank partner [2], so reported FCF overstates the repeatable figure. I no longer use amortization as a reason: MasTec's adj./GAAP gap ($9.30 vs $6.20) is wider than DY's [10]. I do not go below the peer low, because consensus still has ~22% FY28 EPS growth [20] and backlog is a record $12.24B [1]. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Leverage from filings: lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA 2.82x for DY ($2,708.3M / $959.8M) vs 2.12x for MTZ ($2,919.8M / $1,379.5M); 2.58x vs 1.76x ex leases. FY26 top-four customers 57.6% (10-K: AT&T 25.4%, Verizon 14.0%, Lumen 10.8%, Comcast 7.4%); customers may terminate agreements for convenience (10-K Item 1).

thesis_break_reason: $195 is 9.6x my NTM EPS ($20.26), 9.4x the $20.78 FY28 consensus, and 26% below the $263.36 52-week low. At 52% vol a close there would most likely mean the earnings base is breaking, not noise. Likely causes: an FY28 outlook (early Mar 2027) with Communications declining even after the ~$150M wireless recapture; an AT&T or Verizon program cut; Building Systems backlog shrinking as DMV pauses reach awards; or the supplier-finance build reversing and pulling FCF negative. Covenant stress is not a near-term trigger: the maintenance test is 4.50x max consolidated net leverage (4.00x after the step-down) and 2.50x min interest coverage, in compliance with $746.4M revolver availability [2]. The 3.50x senior secured net leverage test I cited in round 1 is real (10-Q [2]) but caps incremental term loans beyond $927M. It limits further debt-funded M&A and is not a default trigger.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my main skeptic finding, and I re-verified it at the source: supplier-finance obligations went from $0 to $367.4M in a year (XBRL [9]). I also confirmed that FY26 OCF included a $223.2M AP increase [5] and that Q4 FY26 FCF of $367.1M [4] came in the same quarter the program began. Two of my round-1 framings were too bearish, and I corrected them. First, the 'hidden ~$160M Communications cut' is ~$150M stated wireless deferral plus only ~$10M underlying ([1] vs [3]), and the Aug guide is still above the March initial guide [4]. I therefore raised underlying FY28 Communications growth from +5% to +6%, still below the ~+7.7% H2 exit rate ex-deferral. Second, the covenant: the maintenance test is 4.50x [2], so covenant stress is out of the thesis-break story. Against the supervisor, I note that the 3.50x senior secured figure does exist in the 10-Q as a limit on incremental facilities; I keep it only as an M&A constraint. I replaced the unverified Weiss MasTec figures with MasTec's own SEC release (Communications margin -170 bp to 8.2%) [10]. I removed the amortization argument for the discount. I dropped Panabee and the Washington Examiner moratorium specifics, and the VIC summary is context only. Valuation: FY28 EPS $18.96 (-9% vs consensus), NTM $20.26 on an earnings-weighted 0.24/0.76 split, x 16x (20% below MTZ, inside the 9-peer range) = $324. EV/EBITDA: $1,130M TTM x 11.1x less ~$2.56B lease-inclusive net debt (horizon notional $2.33B, built on ~$250M underlying FCF, plus $0.23B leases) = $331. Fair value is $327 (from $330). Scenarios: bear $185 / 28% (from 32%, because the cut was mostly deferral and the covenant channel is gone), base $315 / 50%, bull $450 / 22%. Mixture of lognormals (sigmas 0.30/0.20/0.22) plus an 8% wide tail component (sigma 0.8), shaded down 1-2 pts between $242 and $323 for the March reset risk, gives median ~$300, mean ~$320 and P(>= $269.23) = 0.615 (from 0.585). Research was limited to ~10 fetches this round. The 01net copy of MasTec's release returned 403 and I used the SEC copy instead. The Reuters/The Star spectrum article body was not readable statically, so it is not used. Lane share: 13 of 20 research sources are skeptic-lane (65%), 13 of 37 overall including the peer pages.
